Meet your Medical VA

A one-minute introduction to how I support clinics with scheduling, documentation, EHR/EMR entry, and administrative work.

Less time explaining your clinic's terminology and documentation.

A general virtual assistant has to be taught what an MMT grade, a range-of-motion measurement, or a CPT-linked treatment note means before handling your paperwork. As a 4th-year DPT student, I'm already familiar with SOAP notes, evaluations, and progress reports, so I need minimal ramp-up for healthcare terminology and workflows. That means less time spent explaining, fewer terminology mistakes, and fewer corrections.

Every clinic runs differently, so I'll learn your specific systems, templates, and preferences, whether that's WebPT, JaneApp, SimplePractice, or another EHR, and follow them closely. I'm a student, not a licensed clinician, and I don't provide clinical care. I handle the administrative side so your therapists can stay focused on patients, with an assistant who understands why the documentation matters, not just where to type it.

Four services built for outpatient PT and rehab clinics

EHR/EMR Precision Data Entry

Accurate entry of evaluations, daily notes, and discharge summaries, with measurements and terminology checked against the source before anything is saved.

Calendar and Intake Management

Scheduling, reminders, and new-patient intake in JaneApp, SimplePractice, and WebPT, so your front desk has fewer administrative tasks to juggle.

Insurance Prior-Authorization Support

Preparing and submitting authorization requests, tracking status, and flagging denials early so authorizations don't hold up patient visits.

Medically Accurate Health Content Writing

Patient handouts, exercise instructions, and blog posts written from a DPT education, in plain language and ready for clinician review.

Documentation sample

An example of the clinical documentation I work with. This is simulated practice work with no real patient information.

CLINICAL DOCUMENTATION SAMPLE (SIMULATED PRACTICE WORK)

Status: Post-Op Right ACL Reconstruction (Autograft) – Week 8

[SUBJECTIVE] Patient reports to clinic for scheduled rehabilitation session. He states that overall right knee pain has decreased over the past week, currently rated at a 2/10 at rest. Goal for today is to progress single-leg balance and quad activation.

[OBJECTIVE] Active Extension: 0° (Full extension achieved actively). Active Flexion: 120°. Right Quadriceps MMT: 4-/5. Single-leg stance on right lower extremity maintained for 15 seconds.

[ASSESSMENT] Patient is an active 38-year-old male making steady, linear progress through Week 8 of his post-op ACL reconstruction protocol. He demonstrates excellent quad recruitment compared to baseline measurements.

[PLAN] Continue skilled PT 2x/week for next 4 weeks. Progress therapeutic exercises to focus on closed-kinetic chain dynamic movements.

Built around HIPAA privacy standards

Patient data is protected at every step

Secure connections

Work happens on a private, password-protected network. I never use public Wi-Fi to access patient records.

Credential protection

Logins are never shared or stored in plain text. I use two-factor authentication wherever your systems allow it.

Minimum necessary access

I access only the information a task requires. Nothing is downloaded, copied, or kept outside your systems.

Confidentiality agreement

I sign an NDA and will work under a Business Associate Agreement to meet US patient privacy requirements.
